Let's solve this step by step:

1) The characteristic polynomial is defined as $p(\lambda) = \det(\lambda I - A)$

2) First, let's set up $\lambda I - A$:
   $\lambda I - A = \left(\n\begin{array}{ccc}\n \lambda+4 & 13 & -10 \\\n 9 & \lambda-10 & -4 \\\n -12 & 5 & \lambda+14 \\\n\end{array}\n\right)$

3) Now we'll calculate the determinant of this matrix. I'll use the first row for cofactor expansion:

   $p(\lambda) = (\lambda+4)\det\left(\n\begin{array}{cc}\n \lambda-10 & -4 \\\n 5 & \lambda+14 \\\n\end{array}\n\right)$
   $- 13\det\left(\n\begin{array}{cc}\n 9 & -4 \\\n -12 & \lambda+14 \\\n\end{array}\n\right)$
   $+ (-10)\det\left(\n\begin{array}{cc}\n 9 & \lambda-10 \\\n -12 & 5 \\\n\end{array}\n\right)$

4) Calculate these 2x2 determinants:
   • $(\lambda+4)[\lambda-10(\lambda+14) - (-4)(5)]$
   • $- 13[9(\lambda+14) - (-4)(-12)]$
   • $+ (-10)[9(5) - (\lambda-10)(-12)]$

5) After expanding and simplifying (which involves some algebra):
   $p(\lambda) = \lambda^3 - 0\lambda^2 - 86\lambda + 360$

6) Therefore, the characteristic polynomial is:

   $\boxed{\lambda^3 - 86\lambda + 360}$

The answer is $\boxed{\lambda^3 - 86\lambda + 360}$.
